messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Shiny 0.10.0
parts:
Hi all,

We’re hoping to submit Shiny 0.10.0 to CRAN shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we’ve added since 0.9.1. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub (the version number is still 0.9.1.x there but will eventually become 0.10.0 on CRAN):


if (!require('devtools')) install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('rstudio/shiny')

Shiny Docs

Many of you are familiar with knitr and R Markdown, excellent tools for creating documents that combine R code and output with your writing.

With Shiny 0.10 and R Markdown v2, you can easily embed Shiny inputs and outputs, and even entire Shiny applications, right into your R Markdown documents! You can now create documents that allow your readers to change the assumptions underlying your analysis and see the results immediately. R Markdown documents with Shiny apps or widgets embedded are called Shiny Docs.

Shiny Docs combine the expressiveness of R Markdown with the interactivity of Shiny. These documents can be run locally on the desktop or be deployed to ShinyApps or Shiny Server v1.2.

To start writing Shiny Docs, just install the current preview release of RStudio (v0.98.891) as it includes not only updated versions of the various packages required to run Shiny Docs (including Shiny 0.10) but also tools for previewing and iterative development.

Learn more about Shiny Docs here.

Server-side processing for selectize input

The client-side selectize input (introduced in shiny 0.9.0) relies solely on JavaScript to process searching on typing. The server-side selectize input uses R to process searching, and R will return the filtered data to selectize. To use the server version, you need to create a selectize instance in the UI, and update it to the server version:


# in ui.R
selectizeInput('foo', choices = NULL, ...)

# in server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = data, server = TRUE)
})

The server-side processing is particularly useful when the number of choices is very large. For example, when there are 100,000 choices for the selectize input, it will be slow to write and load all of them at once on a page. With the new server-side selectize features, you can start from an empty selectize input, and only fetch the choices that the user searches for, which can be much faster. See this article for more information and examples.

New layout functions

Three new functions, flowLayout(), splitLayout(), and inputPanel(), were added for putting UI elements side by side.

  • flowPanel() lays out its children in a left-to-right, top-to-bottom arrangement.
  • splitLayout() evenly divides its horizontal space among its children (or unevenly divides if cellWidths argument is provided).
  • inputPanel() is like flowPanel(), but with a light grey background, and is intended for encapsulating small input controls wherever vertical space is at a premium.

A new argument inline (TRUE/FALSE) was also added to checkboxGroupInput() and radioButtons() to arrange check boxes and radio buttons horizontally.

Custom validation error messages

Sometimes you do not want your render functions in server.R to proceed unless certain input conditions are satisfied, e.g. the action button has been clicked, or a select input value has been chosen. In these cases, you may want to either stop the render function quietly, or with a custom message. In shiny 0.10.0, we introduced the functions validate() and need() to specify the validation conditions. See this article for details and examples.

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at the NEWS file. Please let us know if you have any comments or questions.

Thanks for your support – we look forward to hearing from you!

messages.author: e569f9ca5b5a4235
messages.subject: Re: Shiny 0.10.0
parts:
Server side selectize really helped me out - I had thousands of options for two of my inputs.  Combined with Joe's leaflet code, I could make my app that explores salary data for different job titles:

http://www.wagemap.com/salaries/

Maybe this is a selectize issue and not a shiny issue, but it's hard to populate the selectizeInput with a default value.  Since the input options aren't updated until after you start typing, it looks like there's only one default option in the drop down, which is misleading.  I made the compromise of just leaving the choices as null, forcing the user to start typing and seeing the whole list.

You guys keep rolling out features just as I need them (datatables also had perfect timing).  Keep up the good work!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny 0.10.0
parts:
After upgrading to shiny 0.10.0, the pages look nicer and being able to use the latest features of DataTables makes a big difference.

One question though. I posted this question on another thread, but I thought I would have the versioning side clarified here:

Is it possible to get DataTables extension TableTools working with shiny 0.10.0? Does the copy of DataTables in shiny include the necessary extensions?

The main reason I would like to have TableTools working is to be able to download data from a DataTables view to Excel, PDF, etc.
Column Reordering and Adding/Removing Columns are two other features that would make a big difference.

Cheers,

Albert.

Server side processing of selectize output is awesome! Use it a lot. I have yet to ty validate() and need() but these are welcome news as my dynamic UI as a lot of cumbersome logics on the server side to make sure that everything is proper before rendering.

Side note: I really really hope that the renderUI() in conjunction with outputUI() are there to stay (they are still marked as tentative/under development functionality). Thanks Shiny team! Love the product and keep up the good work!

Marco
